To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the transnational family communication is mediated through the smartphone, and the smartphone is appropriated in the family communication as a tool to connect the family members.

(a) the smartphone as an assemblagewith its various features and functions, including its portability and its ability to connect to the Internet, is a key factor in the reconfiguration of the transnational family; (b) the smartphone is a tool that enables family members to engage in transnational communication, but it does not necessarily lead to the formation of virtual families; and (c) family communication is mediated through the smartphone, and this mediation is influenced by the norms of family communication
smartphones have been culturally appropriated in the transnational families in the ways that they are used to communicate, to share, to care, and to connect.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the smartphone is culturally appropriated in transnational families.
how mobile technologies are appropriated by transnational families and how the family is (re)imagined through these technologies.
how the smartphone is appropriated and used in the transnational family context.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the smartphone is a powerful tool for the maintenance of family relationships across transnational contexts, but it is not the only or most important tool for this purpose.
smartphones have become a part of the family, and the family is now a part of the smartphone.
the transnational family is reimagining the family through the use of smartphones.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the smartphone is a cultural artefact, which is appropriated by transnational family members to maintain and negotiate family relations in the context of transnationalism.
the smartphone is a key device in the cultural appropriation of ICTs in transnational families.
we have examined how the smartphone is appropriated within the family context, which has been shaped by the historical, social, cultural, economic and technological contexts.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the smartphone, as an ICT, is a social assemblage that is embedded within the cultural and social norms of the family.
the transnational virtual family is a complex assemblage of technologies, norms, and values, and the smartphone is a key player in this assemblage.

transnational families are not merely technologically mediated but also culturally mediated, and that the smartphone is not a mere technological device but a culturally and socially embedded technology that has been appropriated by transnational families in their own way.
